steps.title: The Season 2 Grand Finale!
steps.story: Roll up, roll up! The Idea Pop circus show is tonight, the big finale of Season 2. But there's a problem: the circus star, a little toy acrobat, keeps toppling off the tightrope. Ivy is the show's young engineer, and the crowd is already arriving. Can YOU make a toy acrobat that balances on a string and stays on even after a wobble?

steps.prompt: Do you already have an idea for helping something balance on a thin string?

steps.intro: How does nature keep its balance? Animals stand, climb and leap without toppling over, and people have learned their tricks. Let's meet the balance champions!

clues.text: A cat walking along a narrow fence swings its tail the opposite way when it starts to tip. When a cat falls, it twists its body, with a little help from its tail, so it lands on its feet.
A flamingo can stand on one leg for hours without effort. Its body weight sits right above its foot, and its leg joints lock in place, so it hardly needs its muscles at all.
When a gecko leaps and starts to tip, it swings its tail in mid-air. The swinging tail turns its body back the right way, so it lands safely on a tree trunk.
Human tightrope walkers carry a long pole that often droops down at both ends. The pole puts extra weight low down and spreads it out wide, so wobbles happen slowly and are easy to fix.

steps.secret: Lower the centre of mass! Every object has a balance point called the centre of mass. If it sits above the support, a small wobble makes it fall. But if weight hangs below the support, the object swings back like a pendulum instead of falling. That's why a tightrope walker's drooping pole helps, and why a flamingo keeps its weight right over its foot. Toy makers use this trick in balancing birds that perch on a fingertip.
steps.reveal_hint: Where could you add weight so your acrobat's balance point ends up below the string?

steps.instructions: Make a card acrobat about 8 cm tall and cut a small notch in its feet so it sits on a string. Ask an adult to help with scissors. Stretch a string between two chairs. Try four versions: the plain acrobat, then with a small ball of modelling clay on its head, then on its feet, then on two bent pipe cleaners hanging down below the string, one on each side. Give the string one gentle tap each time and count how many seconds the acrobat stays on.
hints: Use the same amount of clay and the same gentle tap each time, so the test is fair.
Clay on the head makes it worse, because the weight is high up. Clay hanging below the string on bent arms wins, because the balance point drops below the string and the acrobat swings back.

steps.prompt: Draw your acrobat on the tightrope from the front.
steps.guidance: Mark the support point where it touches the string, draw a dot where you think the centre of mass is, and show where you added weight.

steps.instructions: Build your toy acrobat from card, pipe cleaners, modelling clay, coins or beads. Put it on the string, give the string one gentle tap and time how many seconds it stays on. Stop the clock at 60 seconds. Then try a bigger wobble.
test_criteria: How many seconds does your acrobat stay on the string after a wobble?
Does it swing back to upright after the wobble, or tip and fall?
Improve one thing and test again. How many seconds longer does it stay on now?
hints: Watch where it tips. If it falls to one side, the weights aren't even. Make both sides match.
Bend the pipe-cleaner arms down in a big U shape and put the clay or coins at their ends, well below the string. The lower the weight, the stronger the swing back.

steps.celebration_text: The spotlight shines, the drums roll… and your acrobat wobbles, sways and swings right back up! The whole crowd leaps to its feet. That's the grand finale of Season 2! You've finished 20 missions of asking nature and building with your hands: folding, signalling, catching light, outsmarting squirrels and now balancing. Take a bow, Balance Star, and collect your Season 2 medal. See you in the next season!
steps.share_prompt: Share your acrobat and your best balance time on the Ideas Wall for the finale show. Which balance trick from nature was the star of your act?

age_tier_variants.summary: Test where weight helps a toy acrobat balance, then build one that stays on a tightrope after a wobble, for the Season 2 finale.

age_tier_variants.title_override: Biomimicry: Centre of Mass and Stable Equilibrium
age_tier_variants.summary: Explain stable and unstable equilibrium, measure how lowering the centre of mass changes recovery time after a disturbance, and link your design to flamingo posture, gecko tails and tightrope poles.
